items.title: Ford's Backing of Parrish for Mississauga Mayor May Be Working Against Her, New Poll Suggests
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a new Liaison Strategies poll suggests Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie are locked in a dead heat heading into the fall election, even though Ontario Premier Doug Ford has publicly backed Parrish's campaign. The poll, released Friday, found Parrish and Crombie would each take 26 per cent of the vote if the Oct. 26 election were held today, with another 26 per cent of voters still undecided. Councillors Dipika Damerla and Alvin Tedjo trailed with 13 per cent and nine per cent respectively, according to the poll. The Star reports Liaison principal David Valentin said none of the candidates has made a clear case for why voters should choose them over the others, leaving a large pool of undecided voters still up for grabs amid a broader sense the city is heading in the wrong direction. The Star notes an October 2025 Liaison poll also found Crombie and Parrish tied in a then-hypothetical matchup, before Crombie left to lead the Ontario Liberals and later resigned after the party's provincial election loss. Candidate registration for the fall municipal elections opened Friday as well.

items.title: City Warns E-Scooter Injuries Among Mississauga Kids Have Doubled in a Year
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, officials are reminding parents to keep children off e-scooters and e-bikes after a national report found 10 kids died from related injuries across Canada last year, six of them in Ontario. The city cites Canadian Paediatric Surveillance Program data showing 57 severe paediatric cases nationwide in 2025 involving death, an ICU admission or a hospital stay longer than two days, including 12 ICU admissions and 26 hospital stays beyond two days. The City of Mississauga notes e-scooters can be a convenient way for residents and visitors aged 16 and older to get around without a car, helping people connect to transit, school or work. But the city says local emergency department visits involving children aged 15 and under on e-scooters more than doubled between 2023 and 2024, rising from 34 visits to 72. Mississauga officials are using those numbers to urge parents to keep young children off the devices even as their popularity grows.

items.title: Behind the Angled Facade on Mississauga Road: The Leslie Log House Marks 200 Years
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, the Leslie Log House on Mississauga Road is celebrating its 200th anniversary this year, having been built in 1826 by John Leslie Sr. and his wife, Esther Leslie. The outlet reports the house sits at a slight angle to the road, with its front door facing away from traffic, and is surrounded by a remnant orchard left over from the former Riviere Fruit Farm. Modern Mississauga Media notes the building was relocated to its current site in 1994 and is now owned by the City of Mississauga, serving as home to the Streetsville Historical Society and Archives. The outlet's history of the house traces Esther Leslie's own story, noting she was born in 1782 in County Tyrone, Ireland, and first married a man named William Leslie while he was stationed there. Mississauga marked the log house's bicentennial with a public event on Saturday, Aug. 8.

items.title: Mississauga Shelter Staff Say the $25 Adoption Push Isn't Skipping Any Steps
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, staff at Mississauga Animal Services say the screening process for adopting a pet hasn't changed during the shelter's ongoing $25 adoption event, even as the reduced fee draws more interest. The discount, running until Aug. 22 at the shelter's Central Parkway West location, cuts the standard adoption cost from roughly $280 plus tax for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus tax for cats and kittens down to a flat $25. Greg Madeley, the shelter's manager of animal care and wellbeing, told Mississauga.com the lower price is meant to free up kennel space, not shortcut the process of matching an animal with the right home. Mississauga.com reports staff still take steps before an animal leaves the shelter to make sure the pet and the prospective owner are a good fit. Among the animals up for adoption is Kaito, a senior dog who has been at the shelter since July 2023. Mississauga.com notes the shelter has taken in 18,986 animals since 2021.

items.title: Halton Police Say a Mississauga Man Filmed a Woman in an Oakville Fitting Room
items.summary: According to INsauga, Halton Regional Police have charged a Mississauga man after a woman reported being filmed inside a change room at the Winners store on Winston Churchill Boulevard in Oakville on July 22. Police say the woman confronted the man after noticing him, but he fled the store before officers arrived. INsauga reports investigators later identified and arrested the suspect, 34-year-old Jeffrey Abou-Mechrek of Mississauga, charging him with one count of voyeurism. He was released with a future court date in Milton. Police released a photo of Abou-Mechrek because investigators are concerned there may be additional victims they haven't yet identified. Anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has information about the case, is asked to contact Halton's 2 District Criminal Investigations Bureau.
